title: Ibuprofen – Overview
content: Ibuprofen is a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) used to relieve pain, reduce fever, and reduce inflammation. Common brand names include Advil and Motrin. It is available over the counter in 200 mg tablets.

title: Ibuprofen – Side Effects
content: Common side effects of ibuprofen include stomach upset, nausea, vomiting, and heartburn. Serious side effects may include gastrointestinal bleeding, kidney problems, and increased risk of heart attack or stroke with long-term use.

title: Ibuprofen – Dosage
content: For adults and children 12 years and older: take 200–400 mg every 4 to 6 hours while symptoms persist. Do not exceed 1200 mg in 24 hours unless directed by a doctor. Take with food or milk to reduce stomach upset.

title: Acetaminophen – Overview
content: Acetaminophen (paracetamol) is an analgesic and antipyretic medication used to treat mild to moderate pain and fever. Common brand names include Tylenol. It is available over the counter and is considered safe at recommended doses.

title: Acetaminophen – Drug Interaction with Alcohol
content: Drinking alcohol while taking acetaminophen can increase the risk of liver damage. Patients who drink three or more alcoholic beverages per day should ask their doctor before using acetaminophen-containing medicines.

title: Flu Vaccine – Information
content: The annual influenza (flu) vaccine is recommended for everyone 6 months and older. It is the best way to protect against flu and its potentially serious complications. The vaccine is updated each year to match circulating strains.

title: First Aid – Treating Minor Burns
content: For minor burns: cool the burn under cool (not cold) running water for 10–20 minutes. Do not use ice, butter, or toothpaste. Cover loosely with a sterile dressing. Over-the-counter pain relievers may help with pain. Seek medical attention for large, deep, or infected burns.

title: Opioid Overdose – Emergency Response
content: Signs of opioid overdose include slow or stopped breathing, unresponsiveness, and blue lips. Call 911 immediately. Administer naloxone (Narcan) if available. Lay the person on their side (recovery position) to prevent choking. Stay until help arrives.

title: Antibiotic Use – General Guidance
content: Antibiotics should only be used when prescribed by a healthcare professional. Always complete the full course even if you feel better. Never share antibiotics with others. Misuse contributes to antibiotic resistance.

title: Blood Pressure Medications – Overview
content: Common classes of blood-pressure medications include ACE inhibitors (e.g. lisinopril), ARBs (e.g. losartan), beta-blockers (e.g. metoprolol), and calcium channel blockers (e.g. amlodipine). These medications help lower blood pressure and reduce cardiovascular risk.
